clue.text: Do good with second language

parts.note: Hindi is a major language of India

explanation.surface: Advice that a second language does you good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' at the start looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British nouns for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Grow up with short story collection

indicators.note: collection says the gathered letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: short says the word story loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Mature, aided by an anthology of short stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts STORY to STOR, and 'collection' rearranges UP with STOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot up as a new plant does is to grow.

clue.text: Jumping Jack ignored fresh challenge

indicators.note: fresh says the remaining letters take a new order
ignored says that letter is left out of the word jumping

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Jumping Jack Flash ignored, a new challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' drops J from JUMPING, leaving UMPING, which 'fresh' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To call something into question, to dispute its truth, is to challenge it.

clue.text: Frost, say, excelled with pen, revealing deceit

parts.note: Jack Frost is a fictional detective inspector, a DI, in TV's A Touch of Frost
shone means excelled
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A poet such as Frost excelling with the pen, but exposing deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' suggests the poet Robert Frost, but is the British TV detective DI Jack Frost.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceit is lying or cheating, the quality of not being honest.

clue.text: Show amusement about a tiny amount

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the other

parts.note: to grin is to show amusement

explanation.surface: Smiling at how little there is.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain of truth is a very small quantity, a speck.

clue.text: Sauce, when cold, goes in sort of boat

indicators.note: goes in says the pair of pieces is placed inside the rearranged letters
a sort of boat is the word boat in some rearranged form

parts.note: taken as written
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A sauce boat holds sauce, kept cold until served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' gives TABO, and 'goes in' splits it after its third letter; the 'boat' is a red herring for a sauce boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot pepper condiment from Louisiana, an example of a sauce.

clue.text: With respect to novel, it's not to be published

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: About a novel, nothing may be printed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' reads as a book, but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified information is kept secret and must never be made public.

clue.text: Heading for Bristol on one vessel or another

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts one piece above the next
heading for points to the opening letter of Bristol

parts.note: Noah's ark is a vessel

explanation.surface: Heading for Bristol aboard some ship or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the definition: another vessel, after ARK.
explanation.definitionFit: A barque is a type of sailing ship, so another vessel besides the ark.

clue.text: Got cracking with poles not right for airport

indicators.note: not says the right letter is replaced by the poles

parts.note: to get cracking is to start, so got cracking is started
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Started off with ski poles but not right for the airport.
explanation.walkthrough: STANSTED is a London airport in Essex.
explanation.definitionFit: London's third airport, in Essex, is an example of an airport.

clue.text: Show cuckoo a treetop

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go mad and rearrange

explanation.surface: Display a cuckoo up a treetop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuckoo' looks like the bird but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A light comic opera is a type of stage show.

clue.text: Guys possibly helping to make Europe secure

indicators.note: helping to make says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Men lending a hand in securing the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' looks like men, but guys are the lines that hold a tent steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy lines on a tent are cords, so guys are an example of such cords, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: A Greek city seen by Orlando that's very sweet

parts.note: Sparta is the ancient Greek city-state
Orlando is the setter of this puzzle, so the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A visit to a Greek city with the setter is a delight.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters often name themselves in clues; here Orlando stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial sweetener many times sweeter than sugar, so a substance that is intensely sweet.

clue.text: Animal twisted and turned without justification

indicators.note: twisted says the animal's name is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a gnu is an African antelope, the wildebeest
to round or be rounded is to be turned on a lathe, shaped by turning

explanation.surface: An animal writhing and spinning for no apparent reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' reverses GNU to UNG.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim lacking any basis in fact is baseless, having no justification.

clue.text: Visit Bath and Wells?

definitions.meaning: to ... a doctor or a friend is to visit them
Bath and Wells is a Church of England diocese, the seat of a bishop

explanation.surface: A suggestion to go and visit two English towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath and Wells are Somerset towns that together name a diocese, a bishop's area.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's diocese is his see, and to visit someone is to go and see them.

clue.text: Showing up two hours before Cinderella's ragtime ball

parts.note: Cinderella's finery turns back to rags at midnight, so two hours earlier is at ten
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Arriving two hours early for Cinderella's ball to ragtime music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ragtime' is not jazz: it is the time Cinderella returns to rags, midnight.
explanation.definitionFit: Being present at an event is turning up, attendance at it.

clue.text: Withdraw clobber with tears flowing

parts.note: to clobber is to beat or hit hard

indicators.note: flowing says the letters are set loose and rearranged

parts.note: the plural is read as two of the word tear

explanation.surface: An instruction to pull back the clobber, tears running down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' gives two TEARs, which 'flowing' rearranges into A RETREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to pull back from a position, originally a military drumbeat ordering troops to fall back.

clue.text: Jam jar under clothing

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts this piece below the clothing

parts.note: tights are a leg garment
a pot is a jar

explanation.surface: A jam jar tucked beneath clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam jar' reads as one thing; Jam is the definition, a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a jam means being in a difficult situation, a fix.

clue.text: Cheerleader and old boy in wicked tribute

indicators.note: in says the pieces go inside the slang word

parts.note: wicked is slang for excellent, as is ace
the leader, first letter, of cheer
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A cheerleader and an old boy in a naughty tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheerleader' gives the first letter of Cheer, C.
explanation.definitionFit: An award or expression of praise is an honour paid, a tribute.

clue.text: Discover small donkey abroad

parts.note: moke is British slang for a donkey
abroad means out and about, as news is out

explanation.surface: Finding a little donkey overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: MOKE is an old British slang word for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To force something hidden into the open is to uncover or discover it.

clue.text: Song written by Lennon for group

definitions.meaning: a 1969 Beatles song written by John Lennon, opening Abbey Road
to group is to gather or assemble as one

explanation.surface: A Lennon song written for his band.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles track title, and also a verb phrase meaning to gather or unite.

clue.text: Female rugby sides? See play

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: sides points to the outermost letters of rugby

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: Women's rugby teams worth a look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides' looks like teams but means the two ends of 'rugby'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's history about the victor of Agincourt is an example of a play.

clue.text: Go on without PR for scary female

indicators.note: without says those two letters are removed

parts.note: to progress is to go on, advance

explanation.surface: Carry on without publicity for a frightening woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A female monster from fairy tales, a frightening woman.

clue.text: It's all right hugging a tree

indicators.note: hugging says one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: OK means all right, acceptable

explanation.surface: Reassurance that it is fine to hug a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A common broad-leaved hardwood, an example of a tree.

clue.text: Writer of Swedish series about doctor — originally British medical drama series

indicators.note: about says the series word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a string of events is a series of them

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word doctor

parts.note: ER was a long-running American hospital television drama

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian writer of a series about a doctor, first a British medical drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the series word round the rest; ER was in fact an American drama, so 'British' only gives B.
explanation.definitionFit: August Strindberg was a Swedish playwright and novelist, writing in that language.

clue.text: Patriarch — one with article in pouch

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in says the article goes inside the pouch

parts.note: a sac is a pouch in an animal or plant
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A patriarch carrying one item in his bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham's son, one of the founding fathers of Israel, a patriarch.

clue.text: Song about Republican in Alaska, primarily

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A song about a Republican from Alaska.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo song in an opera is an example of a song.

clue.text: Strange approach with yearbooks

indicators.note: strange says the letters are made odd, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd way of going about yearbooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yearbooks' must be split: 'year' gives Y and 'books' is the definition. 'Strange' scrambles APPROACH with Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective name for writings excluded from the canonical Bible, a set of books.

clue.text: Tongue put right into bouquet

indicators.note: into says one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its nose, its aroma

explanation.surface: Putting your tongue right into a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' looks like flowers but means a wine's aroma.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of medieval Scandinavia, and 'tongue' is an old word for language.

clue.text: Additional empty chest in passage

parts.note: extra means additional

indicators.note: empty says the inside of the word chest is removed, leaving its outside

explanation.surface: An extra chest with nothing in it sitting in a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' looks like a corridor but is a passage of text.
explanation.definitionFit: A section quoted from a book or document is a passage taken from it.

clue.text: Anne's place keeps last of banana splits

indicators.note: keeps says the place name holds another letter inside it

parts.note: Anne of Cleves, fourth wife of Henry VIII, came from Cleves in Germany

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of banana

explanation.surface: Anne's home keeps banana splits, a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banana splits' reads as the dessert, but 'splits' is a verb and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave something is to split it, as with an axe.
